title: crypto2dev_cipher: AES-CBC post-encrypt reg update uses cast-away-const
description: In crypto2dev_cipher(), aes is declared 'const Aes*'. The CBC post-encrypt update writes to aes->reg via '(byte*)((Aes*)aes)->reg' — casting away const to write. This is undefined behavior in C89/C99 (writing through a pointer derived from a const-qualified pointer to an object that was originally declared non-const is defined; writing to an object that was originally declared const is UB). The wc_CryptoInfo struct carries 'const Aes*' for cipher operations, so the original object may or may not have been declared const. The compiler is permitted to optimize away this store or generate a SIGBUS on read-only-mapped memory. The fix is for aes to be non-const in cipher(), which requires matching the info struct field type — or using info->cipher.aescbc.aes directly (which has the same type). Also applies to AES-CTR reg update.
